_what: Synthetic Dart closure-binder gate for #3903 (DART-11), following bench/ruby-gem-resolution and bench/dart-deferred-imports: exact accuracy cells and fingerprints, scaling ratios against input and output growth, and an operation count for the enclosing-type search (#3912 review). Real capture emitter, real parse worker (dist/), real Dart ScopeResolver and pubspec loader; analyze, persistence and full-pipeline memory are outside this benchmark.
_triage: Shape and fingerprint failures are deterministic: inspect the corpus and the resolved edges, never rebaseline just to make CI green. The runner also fails, before any baseline comparison, when a function misses an expected CALLS edge or gains one the source never makes. An operation-count failure is deterministic too: a capture pass stepped onto more ancestors than the budget allows, so some lookup climbs the tree again. For a timing failure, rerun on an idle machine and verify the report shows its profile (ci: 5 interleaved samples after 1 warmup; full: 15 after 2) before investigating a regression. Millisecond observations are context, not gates.
_shape_note: Exact counts are the workload FLOOR. small = 32 functions x 3 closures, large = 512 x 3 (functions 16x), dense = 32 x 48 (closures per function 16x; in `nested`, nesting depth 16x). Nested closures are indented by a fixed width, so input bytes grow linearly with depth (#3912 review: the old indentation grew quadratically). Each cell records its input bytes and its emitted output (capture groups, Function scopes, relationships, CALLS edges, declines). Expected edges per function are computed from the binder rule, not read back from the graph: an untyped rebinding `(cs)` declines (`receiver-type-unresolved/untyped-binder`), a typed `(Other cs)` reaches Other.save, and `(x) { cs.run(); }` reaches the nearest `cs` (the `Address` parameter side by side, the enclosing `Other cs` when nested).
_fingerprint_note: Recorded on main e2b7cdbd0. Hashes pin every relationship (endpoints, type, confidence, reason) and every decline (reason/detail, file, name, position). #3917 (the enclosing-type fix) produces identical cells: it changes no output.
_scaling_note: Scaling ratios are (t_big / t_small) / growth, where growth is the larger of the input-byte, capture-group and relationship growth between the two cells: about 1 is linear in input plus output, about 16 is quadratic at these sizes. Every gated ratio's budget is 1.5 (bench/scope-capture); there is no allowance for nesting depth. nested_resolve_closure_scaling_ratio is reported, not gated (_resolve_depth_note).
_operations_note: Under --check each workload's capture pass counts the ancestors the enclosing-type search steps onto (getDartEnclosingTypeStats, #3917): at most one per Function scope. #3917 reads the enclosing type from the capture walk for every closure and memoises a declared member's lookup, so the count stays below one per scope at any depth (0.02-0.29 here). A tree without the counter fails the check rather than passing it.
_depth_note: Capture is gated over nesting depth 3 -> 48 at 1.5. On main it fails at 11.2-11.6: three per-closure or per-call walks made it O(depth^2), the enclosing-type climb and the Dart callable-flow hooks' parent and sibling reads (#3917) and the shared operand search of every closure argument (#3920). node-tree-sitter's `parent` and sibling reads re-descend from the root, about 150 ns per AST level, so any helper that calls them once per node grows with depth. This gate passes only once that repeated work is gone; it is not budgeted around.
_resolve_depth_note: nested_resolve_closure_scaling_ratio is reported, not gated: 3.26 on main (3.11 in a second run) over depth 3 -> 48. Resolution code is unchanged by #3917 and #3920 (the captures are identical), and the term is the shared lexical lookup: lookupLexicalName, reached through lookupNameClaim mostly from emitReceiverBoundCalls, climbs the scope chain from each reference to its binder, O(depth) per reference. It is open and shared, not Dart's, and is tracked in #3915; a 1.5 gate on it would fail on every tree until that lookup changes.
_negative_controls_note: Control A, a climb to the root per closure (the main shape, with the counter added), fails the operation budget deterministically: 'sibling_small: enclosing-type search stepped onto 3206 ancestors for 516 Function scopes'. Control B, scanning every registered scope per binder (O(binders x scopes)), moved the 16x function ratio to 1.57 against 1.39 for clean code in one run, but clean code read 1.64 on the closure axis in the same run: on a busy host the ratios at these sizes move by about +-0.25, so timing does not reliably catch control B. Operation counts are the reliable regression signal; the timing ratios catch only large super-linear terms.
_profiles_note: Two profiles share the shapes and every accuracy gate. CI (the default, and what --check runs in the benchmarks job): one process, one parse worker, every workload timed, min of 5 after 1 warmup, interleaved. --full: one child times every workload, min of 15 after 2 warmups, and each shape runs in a fresh child for its peak RSS. Wall times are in _measured_ci.

_measured_ci.environment: macOS arm64 / Node 24.16.0, 2026-11-13, main e2b7cdbd0, shared host (load average 21-44 on 15 cores)
_measured_ci.operations: unavailable on main (no counter); --check reports each cell as a failure

_measured_note: One CI-profile run on main. Its ratios are the failures this gate exists to catch, recorded so the fixes have a before. Exact shapes and fingerprints are identical on #3917.
